data.title: WSFS outlines 45%-50% deposit beta in current hiking cycle while targeting double-digit Walton Trust growth
Primis signals 8%–8.5% year-end balance sheet growth as it targets TCE north of 8.5% in a few quarters
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Primis Financial Corp. (FRST) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "For the quarter, we're reporting $8.7 million of net earnings or about $0.35 per share" and "our net interest margin coming out of the Community Bank... increased to about 3.66%" (President, CEO & Director Dennis Zember).

  • "On the negative side, we had a falloff in revenue in the mortgage company" after "the 10-year treasury increased almost 100 basis points in the third quarter"; "if these higher rates were to persist, we think annual volume would decrease from about $1.6 billion a year to about $1.1 billion a year" and the company has "reduced fixed costs by about $4 million a year" (President, CEO & Director Zember).

  • "We ended the quarter with about $3.5 billion in loans" and "I'd expect balances to come in a little in the fourth quarter"; "I expect that we probably finish the year with total growth in the balance sheet of about 8% to 8.5% on year-end balances" (President, CEO & Director Zember).

  • "Tangible book value ended at $13.81" and "our TCE ratio improved to 8.14%"; "Matt and I really would like for TCE to be north of 8.5%" (President, CEO & Director Zember).

  • "Primis reported earnings of $8.7 million or diluted earnings per share of $0.35 in the third quarter compared to $9.4 million or $0.38 per share in the second quarter" (Executive VP & CFO Matthew Switzer).

Outlook

  • "I think we'll continue to see some incremental margin expansion" and "we'll have some incremental margin expansion 4 or 5 basis points over time" (Executive VP & CFO Switzer).

  • "I'd expect balances to come in a little in the fourth quarter, just given the mortgage backdrop and how that's going to affect warehouse" (President, CEO & Director Zember).

  • "I think for the year, we're going to end up with loan growth in probably the 8% category" and "I think we can probably sustain that for a couple of more years" (President, CEO & Director Zember).

  • "I think we'll be flattish in the fourth quarter and then start to tick down in Q1" on expenses, and "we continue to expect approximately $3 million of annualized savings from vendor consolidation and statement services beginning early in 2027" (Executive VP & CFO Switzer).

Financial Results

  • "Net interest income was approximately $36.3 million" and "our reported net interest margin was 3.66%, up 21 basis points linked quarter" (Executive VP & CFO Switzer).

  • "Noninterest income was $12.9 million in the third quarter versus $22 million last quarter" and "mortgage banking revenue was $8 million, down from $11.4 million last quarter" (Executive VP & CFO Switzer).

  • "Primis Mortgage still closed $347 million of volume" and "we also reported $1.5 million of gain on sale income related to Panacea loans and the guaranteed portion of SBA loans" (Executive VP & CFO Switzer).

  • "Our provision this quarter was $1.1 million compared to $5.5 million in the second quarter" and "asset quality remains stable with nonperforming assets... improving to 1.43% of total assets" (Executive VP & CFO Switzer).

Q&A

  • Russell Gunther, Stephens: asked whether margin expansion continues into Q4/next year; Executive VP & CFO Switzer said "we'll continue to see some incremental margin expansion" and framed it as "4 or 5 basis points over time" driven by loan repricing and restrained deposit betas.

  • Russell Gunther, Stephens: pressed for the core expense run-rate and timing of efficiency actions; Executive VP & CFO Switzer said a "run rate expense" around "$22 million to $22.5 million quarterly" remains the baseline, with savings beginning "midway through the first quarter" and the "$3 million" statement/vendor action "incrementally bringing down that $22.5 million number."

  • Chase (for Stephen Moss), Raymond James: asked where growth opportunities are and how to think about 4Q and 2027; President, CEO & Director Zember said "the core bank may be flat in the fourth quarter" due to "one big loan payoff" and reiterated "we're going to end up with loan growth in probably the 8% category," while Executive VP & CFO Switzer said the core bank is viewed as "up 5% to 7% year in and year out."

  • Chase (for Stephen Moss), Raymond James: asked loan pricing; management said "Panacea is probably 5-year plus 225, 250" and "warehouse is generally like with fees generally like SOFR plus 275, maybe 300" (President, CEO & Director Zember).

  • Chase (for Stephen Moss), Raymond James: asked upside if mortgage rates fall; President, CEO & Director Zember said at "7%, 7.25%" Primis is "about $1.1 billion mortgage shop" and at mid-6% rates "on track to do $1.6 billion, $1.7 billion," adding "we're sort of presuming that these rates will be persistent" while adjusting costs.

  • Christopher Marinac, Brean Capital: asked about the rebranded Banking Valet deposit channel; President, CEO & Director Zember described it as "our proprietary app" and said "probably half of our checking accounts are rooted with this app" and "virtually, every commercial deposit relationship we have... came because of its service."

  • Christopher Marinac, Brean Capital: asked whether credit could improve further; Executive VP & CFO Switzer said "we didn't have any migration in the quarter," and President, CEO & Director Zember said the company may consider charge-offs vs. specific reserves on classified assets "before the end of the quarter."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst tone was slightly positive, with repeated validation of core performance ("great core result this quarter"; "still an excellent result") but persistent probing on margin durability, expense trajectory, and credit normalization (Russell Gunther, Stephens; Christopher Marinac, Brean Capital).

  • Management tone was positive in prepared remarks ("healthy increase"; "capital levels are creeping up") and measured in Q&A, emphasizing control levers ("we have been selectively adjusting rates"; "we're taking steps to align costs") while avoiding precise long-range goalposts ("it wouldn't be normal for me to tell you the next goal") (President, CEO & Director Zember; Executive VP & CFO Switzer).

  • Versus the prior quarter’s more “stable results/operating leverage” framing, this call’s tone leaned more execution-and-environment-aware, with mortgage volatility and specific cost-rightsizing emphasized (President, CEO & Director Zember).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Margin commentary shifted from Q2’s "plus or minus a basis point or 2 is probably where we'll be for the foreseeable future" (Executive VP & CFO Switzer, Q2) to Q3’s "continue to see some incremental margin expansion" with "4 or 5 basis points over time" (Executive VP & CFO Switzer, Q3).

  • Mortgage discussion moved from Q2 highlighting "the best quarter we've ever had in mortgage" (President, CEO & Director Zember, Q2) to Q3 describing a rate-driven reset, including "annual volume would decrease from about $1.6 billion a year to about $1.1 billion a year" and a division loss that included pipeline valuation impacts (President, CEO & Director Zember, Q3).

  • Operating leverage initiatives remained a through-line: Q2 laid out "about $7 million pretax" next-year impact from the consolidation project (President, CEO & Director Zember, Q2), while Q3 reiterated near-term execution timing, including "approximately $3 million of annualized savings... beginning early in 2027" and "start to tick down in Q1" (Executive VP & CFO Switzer, Q3).

Risks and Concerns

  • "There's real competition out there right now on the loan side" and deposit growth has been intentionally restrained because management "did want to outrun the Fed" and instead "rely more heavily on FHLB" (President, CEO & Director Zember).

  • Mortgage rate sensitivity was positioned as the key earnings swing factor, with mitigation centered on cost actions: "we have been rightsizing costs" and "reduced fixed costs by about $4 million a year" (President, CEO & Director Zember).

  • Credit risk monitoring remained focused on existing problem assets: "It's really focused on working through the ones we already have" and the company debated charge-offs vs. carrying specific reserves (Executive VP & CFO Switzer; President, CEO & Director Zember).

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 around continued core-bank margin expansion, stable credit, and a more rate-pressured mortgage backdrop being addressed through cost rightsizing. Leadership reiterated an expectation for year-end balance sheet growth of about 8%–8.5% and emphasized building capital toward a tangible common equity ratio north of 8.5% over the next few quarters, while pointing to early-2027 vendor and statement-service savings as a key operating leverage catalyst.

data.title: Autoliv signals $1.2b operating cash flow and ~10.5% adjusted operating margin for 2026 while cutting CapEx to ~4% of sales
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Autoliv (ALV) Q3 2026

Management view

  • "We delivered a strong third quarter in a tough environment with adjusted operating margin exceeding our earlier indications" (President, CEO, Member of Research Advisory Board & Director Mikael Bratt), adding that "the progress we achieved during the quarter reinforces our confidence in further profitability improvement through year-end."

  • "In China, we once again outperformed light vehicle production, driven by strong growth with Chinese OEMs" (President, CEO Bratt), and "in India, we grew sales by nearly 30% organically," while also stating: "Adjusted operating margin reached 9.7%, ahead of earlier indication."

  • "In the quarter, we repurchased over 1.2 million shares for USD 150 million and paid dividends of USD 63 million" (President, CEO Bratt), while reiterating: "we reiterate our full year 2026 guidance of flat organic sales with continued significant outperformance of light vehicle production."

  • "We have narrowed down our adjusted operating margin guidance to be around 10.5%, which is at the low end of the range of around 10.5% to 11%" (President, CEO Bratt), and "CapEx is now expected to be around 4% of sales compared with the previous expectations of less than 5% of sales."

  • "Our net sales were $2.7 billion" and "the adjusted earnings per share diluted decreased by $0.13 to $2.19" (Executive VP of Finance & CFO Monika Grama), while noting the gap between reported and adjusted operating income was "mainly related to capacity alignment activities."

Outlook

  • "Mobility Global now expects global light vehicle production to decline by 1.9% in 2026" (President, CEO Bratt), and "for the fourth quarter, Mobility Global forecast global light vehicle production to decline by approximately 4.5% year-over-year," including "a 9% decline" for China.

  • "We expect our financial performance to strengthen in the fourth quarter versus the third quarter" (President, CEO Bratt), citing "higher sales volumes, increased engineering income and customer compensation related to raw material inflation" plus "greater automization and digitalization."

  • "Since then, the business has faced additional headwinds amounting to approximately 170 to 180 basis points" (President, CEO Bratt), and "through disciplined execution of these initiatives, we expect to offset most of the incremental headwinds."

  • Change vs. last quarter: in Q2, management said, "We continue to expect an adjusted operating margin of around 10.5% to 11%" (President, CEO Bratt); in Q3, management tightened language to "around 10.5%, the low end of our range" (President, CEO Bratt).

Financial results

  • "Gross profit decreased by $26 million with the gross margin declining from 19.3% to 18.4%" (President, CEO Bratt), while also stating, "Adjusted operating income for the third quarter decreased by 3% to USD 262 million" and "Operating cash flow was USD 239 million."

  • "The driver behind the lower gross profit was mainly the $12.5 million supplier compensation in 2025" plus "higher costs for raw materials" (CFO Grama), and "raw material costs had a gross negative impact of $42 million in the quarter."

  • "During the quarter, we achieved customer compensation covering more than 80% of tariff costs" (CFO Grama), while also saying, "tariff-related headwinds still reduced our adjusted operating margin by around 35 basis points."

  • "Free operating cash flow was positive $124 million" and "the cash conversion was 80%, in line with our target of at least 80%" (CFO Grama).

Q&A

  • Gautam Narayan, RBC Capital Markets: "some color on the EMEA underperformance in the quarter?" Title Last Name: "there are elements of customer mix" and "I should not read into much into those swings you see there," adding, "we emphasize more the overall market share development and outperformance here than the regional shifts."

  • Gautam Narayan, RBC Capital Markets: "how we should think about the raw material cost increase bleeding into '27" Title Last Name: "we expect it to be as challenging in 2027 as it has been in 2026" and "no headwind or tailwind coming from that."

  • Emmanuel Rosner, Wolfe Research: "the implied fourth quarter outlook implied by your guidance" and whether recoveries are "already secured" Title Last Name: "we move into the fourth quarter here with confidence" and "we have a good activity plan for the fourth quarter."

  • Emmanuel Rosner, Wolfe Research: China exports exposure and potential restrictions Title Last Name: "we don't have a separate supply chain for the export vehicles or the domestic vehicles" and "with our footprint, we can support a customer that wants or forced to localize rather than to export from another region."

  • Chris McNally, Evercore ISI: whether China organic growth could "go sort of back to positive" and longer-term growth Title Last Name: "I have great confidence" and "we are on a good trajectory with the Chinese OEMs and expect it to continue to grow."

  • Chris McNally, Evercore ISI: how much of inflation headwinds tied to Thailand flooding/logistics CFO Grama: "Connected to the Thailand flooding, we see -- we can call it not material impact" and on logistics "double-digit cost increases" with "logistic optimization initiatives" and "a cost very difficult to pass on."

  • Yan Dong, Deutsche Bank: why guidance narrows to low end and 2027 carryover Title Last Name: "the higher-than-expected cost pressure" and for 2027 "we expect that to continue to be some headwinds."

  • Yan Dong, Deutsche Bank: safety switch business outside vehicles Title Last Name: "we are also growing this business as we speak" but "we have decided and elected not to give too much details and numbers at this point."

  • Jose Asumendi, JPMorgan: 2027 launches and Europe stoppages Title Full Name (Vice President of Investor Relations Anders Trapp): "we expect to see a higher number of launches in 2027" and on stoppages "no visibility or indications at this point in time."

  • Stephen Benhamou, BofA Securities: Q4 outperformance confidence and margin downside scenarios Title Last Name: "the momentum carries through into Q4" and on margin floor "it depends... on the external circumstances here."

  • Unknown Analyst, TD Cowen: whether mitigation is a pull-forward Title Last Name: "I would say no," adding, "it's a constant work on all that." Unknown Analyst: CapEx sustainability CFO Grama: "it's a phasing of activities" and "we prefer to prioritize activities that have a higher payback."

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts: slightly negative to pressing, with repeated challenges on Q4 implied margin/step-up and China/top-line mechanics, including "a very high margin around 14% or so" (Emmanuel Rosner, Wolfe Research) and "what gives you confidence into this acceleration?" (Stephen Benhamou, BofA Securities).

  • Management: slightly positive and execution-focused in prepared remarks ("we delivered a strong third quarter" (President, CEO Bratt)), and firm but cautious in Q&A, frequently anchoring to plans and uncertainty ("we move into the fourth quarter here with confidence" (President, CEO Bratt); "it depends... on the external circumstances" (President, CEO Bratt)).

  • Versus last quarter: Q2 tone emphasized "record second quarter" and "solid momentum" (President, CEO Bratt), while Q3 added more explicit constraint language ("low end" of the range (President, CEO Bratt)) and more Q&A focus on Q4 implied profitability and China/export dynamics.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Guidance language tightened: Q2 said "around 10.5% to 11%" (President, CEO Bratt), while Q3 shifted to "around 10.5%, the low end" (President, CEO Bratt), alongside CapEx moving from "below 5% of sales" (President, CEO Bratt, Q2) to "around 4% of sales" (President, CEO Bratt, Q3).

  • China mix continued to rise, with Q2 stating "the Chinese OEMs accounted for 55% of our sales in China" (President, CEO Bratt) versus Q3 stating "Chinese OEMs accounted for 58% of our sales in China" (President, CEO Bratt).

  • Strategic emphasis shifted from footprint restructuring in Q2 ("gradually discontinue our manufacturing operations in Turkey" (President, CEO Bratt)) to China expansion and product platforming in Q3 ("opened our second R&D center in China" and "launched the human body Model Safety Suite" (President, CEO Bratt)).

Risks and concerns

  • "Call-off accuracy has deteriorated somewhat" (President, CEO Bratt), and management framed execution risk as: "Maintaining high call-off accuracy remains critical" (President, CEO Bratt).

  • "We are closely monitoring the potential impact of geopolitical developments in the Middle East" (President, CEO Bratt), describing effects on "supply chains, raw material costs and overall vehicle demand."

  • "Raw material costs had a gross negative impact of $42 million" (CFO Grama) and management highlighted incomplete tariff offset: "customer compensation covering more than 80% of tariff costs" (CFO Grama).

Final takeaway

Management reiterated flat organic sales and $1.2 billion operating cash flow expectations for 2026, while tightening adjusted operating margin expectations to around 10.5% (low end) and lowering CapEx to around 4% of sales. The call highlighted continued China and India momentum—particularly growth with Chinese OEMs—and positioned Q4 as a seasonally stronger quarter supported by higher volumes, engineering income, and customer compensation, while repeatedly pointing to ongoing headwinds from raw materials, logistics, and geopolitical uncertainty.

data.title: Comfort Systems targets mid-20% same-store revenue growth in 2027 as backlog reaches $17.8B
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Comfort Systems USA (FIX) Q3 2026

Management View

  • CEO Brian Lane said results “exceed even our recent record results,” highlighting “$13.91 per share,” backlog “grew to a new high of $17.8 billion,” and “an eighth consecutive sequential backlog increase” (CEO Brian Lane).
  • Lane announced two acquisitions and shareholder returns, saying, “I’m happy to announce the acquisition of two companies on August 1. Boys Electrical… and NeoPod,” adding “we increased our quarterly dividend by $0.10 to $1 per share, and we actively purchased shares during the quarter” (CEO Lane).
  • Lane disclosed a CFO transition: “Last night, we announced Bill’s decision to retire…,” and “Julie will be promoted to CFO as Bill’s successor” (CEO Lane).
  • CFO William George framed succession and acquisition continuity, stating, “Comfort Systems will still have the best CFO in construction,” and emphasizing, “we refuse to be hurried” in M&A (Executive VP & CFO William George).
  • George reported the quarter’s headline financials: “revenue… was $3.8 billion,” “gross profit was $934 million,” “operating income… was $625 million,” and “net income… was $489 million or $13.91 per share” (Executive VP & CFO William George).
  • President Trent McKenna highlighted demand and mix, saying “technology… was 59% of our revenue,” modular was “17% of our revenue” year-to-date, and “service revenue was higher by 13% this quarter” (President Trent McKenna).

Outlook

  • Management said, “we expect continuing growth and strong results for the remainder of 2026 and 2027” (CEO Brian Lane).
  • George provided explicit growth and margin expectations: “we expect full year same-store revenue will also be in the mid-40% range,” “same-store full year 2027 revenue will grow in the mid-20% range,” and “we currently expect that 2027 gross profit margins are likely to continue in the strong ranges that we’ve achieved” (Executive VP & CFO William George).
  • On capacity investment cadence, George said, “we estimate that full year CapEx will be 4% to 5% of revenue,” and “we’re likely to continue to incur CapEx at elevated levels during the first half of 2027” (Executive VP & CFO George).
  • Compared with last quarter, management raised its 2026 same-store growth language from “mid- to high 30% range” in Q2 to “mid-40% range” in Q3, and expanded modular capacity commentary from “approximately 5 million square feet… by late summer 2027” in Q2 to “approximately 6 million square feet… by the end of 2027” in Q3 (Executive VP & CFO William George; President Trent McKenna).

Financial Results

  • George said segment growth was driven by both platforms: “Electrical segment revenue grew by 85% and mechanical revenue grew by 43%” (Executive VP & CFO William George).
  • Profitability commentary centered on stability at high levels: “gross profit percentage remained consistent… at 24.8%,” while “margins in our electrical segment slipped to 24.3%… as compared to 26.2%” last year, which he attributed to prior-year “discrete gains” (Executive VP & CFO George).
  • Cash generation and working capital were notable: “Free cash flow for the third quarter of 2026 was $806 million,” aided by “favorable collections from large technology customers” and “$166 million in income tax payments that we were able to defer” (Executive VP & CFO William George).
  • Capital returns and investment were both active: “we invested over $100 million in CapEx to expand prefabrication facilities,” and “year-to-date, we’ve returned $349 million to our shareholders, and we’ve retired approximately 212,000 shares” (Executive VP & CFO George).

Q&A

  • Adam Thalhimer, Thompson, Davis: asked about “sequential margin decline”; President McKenna said, “we carried a higher proportion of equipment and materials… equipment doesn’t carry the margin,” and CFO George added purchase accounting “adjustments were like $12 million higher… a straight hit to margins,” while also calling the quarter “definitely early in jobs” (President Trent McKenna; Executive VP & CFO William George).
  • Adam Thalhimer, Thompson, Davis: asked whether awards were from “traditional data center customers” or “new customers”; McKenna said “there are definitely new customers creeping in” and framed the constraint as “labor,” while Lane pointed to “repeat business from very sophisticated customers” (President McKenna; CEO Brian Lane).
  • Adam Bubes, Goldman Sachs: pressed on modular expansion and new customer engagement; McKenna said the “6 million… is based on our current programmatic build-outs,” and George added, “we haven’t yet reached terms where we’re willing to accept business,” citing “the ability to pay” and 5-year volume commitments for programmatic deals (President Trent McKenna; Executive VP & CFO William George).
  • Sangita Jain, KeyBanc: asked about backlog mix and duration; George said backlog is “really lumpy,” while Lane said durations are “roughly 18 to 24 months” as project size rises (Executive VP & CFO George; CEO Brian Lane).
  • Brent Thielman, Oppenheimer: asked about customer financing risk and power availability; George described evaluating counterparties and lien rights (“the right to seize the building if we don’t get paid”), and Lane said prospects typically have power “already solved,” adding, “it really hasn’t delayed anything we’re seeing yet” (Executive VP & CFO George; CEO Brian Lane).
  • Timothy Mulrooney, William Blair: asked about data center moratorium rhetoric and modular customer concentration; George said “generally no” project impacts, while Lane added, “we have not been delayed by any moratorium,” and George explained modular focus: “why would we divert from a sure thing to sort of a mystery” (Executive VP & CFO George; CEO Brian Lane).
  • Kurt Yinger, D.A. Davidson: asked whether outsized bookings pull forward demand and about capital deployment; George said there’s “no gauge” on capacity but conditions are “extremely supportive,” and on buybacks, “we typically use 15% to 20% of our free cash flow to buy shares,” plus “we will not do a deal just because we have money” (Executive VP & CFO George).

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive, mixing praise (“Congrats on another great quarter”) with repeated diligence on margins, backlog duration, customer financing, moratorium/power risks, and modular customer concentration (multiple analysts).
  • Management’s tone was positive and confident in demand and execution, with defensive precision on forward margin assumptions: “we do not represent that margins will go up in the future,” while maintaining conviction that business conditions remain strong (Executive VP & CFO William George).
  • Versus last quarter, management introduced a major leadership transition (CFO retirement and successor named) and spent more time on counterparty/payment scrutiny; analyst questioning intensified around financing, moratoriums, and backlog duration compared with Q2’s emphasis on modular capacity build-out and cash flow mechanics (CEO Brian Lane; Executive VP & CFO William George).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Backlog rose to “$17.8 billion” in Q3 from “$14.1 billion” in Q2, and management framed Q3 as an “eighth consecutive sequential backlog increase,” while Q2 emphasized reaching the first “quarterly revenue… exceeded $3 billion” (CEO Brian Lane).
  • Guidance language firmed up on growth: Q2 expected 2026 same-store growth “mid- to high 30%,” while Q3 said 2026 same-store growth “mid-40%,” and added a quantified 2027 same-store view of “mid-20%” (Executive VP & CFO William George).
  • Modular expansion timeline increased: Q2 guided to “approximately 5 million square feet… by late summer 2027,” while Q3 guided to “approximately 6 million square feet of capacity by the end of 2027” (President Trent McKenna).
  • Analyst focus expanded from Q2’s cash flow and modular backlog mechanics to Q3’s margin mix drivers, backlog duration, customer financing, and regulatory rhetoric; management repeatedly returned to labor planning discipline and customer quality screens (Executive VP & CFO George; President McKenna).

Risks and Concerns

  • Labor availability was described as the limiting factor: “the governor isn’t demand, the governor is really just labor,” with management emphasizing labor planning before accepting work (President Trent McKenna).
  • Margin variability risk was tied to project mix and stage: “early in jobs,” higher “equipment and materials” mix, and acquisition-related “purchase adjustments” flowing through cost (Executive VP & CFO William George).
  • Customer/counterparty risk in modular and large projects was explicitly addressed through payment structures and selectivity: “front and center for us is the ability to pay,” including situations requiring “very special terms” (Executive VP & CFO George).
  • Political/regulatory headlines were discussed as a monitoring item; management said no observed project delays: “I don’t know a project where one of these considerations has changed its trajectory,” and “we have not been delayed by any moratorium” (Executive VP & CFO George; CEO Brian Lane).

Final Takeaway

Comfort Systems’ management tied Q3 performance to sustained technology-driven construction demand, record backlog, and continuing modular and prefabrication investment, while signaling elevated but variable margins due to mix and job stage effects. Leadership change was a central new development, with Bill George set to retire after 2026 results and Julie Shaeff named CFO successor, as management reiterated discipline on labor planning, counterparty strength, and selective acceptance of new modular programmatic relationships.

data.title: BP, Louisiana reach deal to accelerate Deepwater Horizon payments
data.description:
BP (BP) said Friday it reached an agreement with the state of Louisiana to provide an accelerated, lump-sum $350M payment to resolve claims over the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill and settle remaining coastal zone lawsuits brought by Louisiana parishes.

Louisiana had been owed $373M ‌over ⁠the next seven years, but the state will now receive a single $350M payment under the new agreement.

"We have now disposed of ​claims and settled with all ​but ⁠one of the major defendants in these coastal cases," Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry ​said.

BP (BP) said it remains a significant energy investor in the state, where it spent $590M with Louisiana vendors and paid more than $280M in royalties and property and franchise taxes in 2025.

data.title: Gold settles below $4,000 after steepest weekly loss in nearly five months
data.description:
Gold futures fell to three-month lows and silver slumped to its lowest level in nearly a year on ‌Friday, as higher energy prices added to inflation concerns and reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain restrictive monetary policy.

Brent crude oil closed at its highest level in six months as as Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia continued to raise concerns over further disruption to energy supplies and traders bet on renewed fighting in the Middle East after the U.S. midterm election on November 3.

The selloff in tech stocks has also led to margin calls for ​equity traders and investors, causing them to sell gold and silver assets, American Gold Exchange analyst Jim Wyckoff said in a note.

"A rising inflation backdrop along with selling pressure to cover losses in equity or bond market positions is a negative combination for gold in the short-term, even as the Fed is looking assured to keep rates unchanged at next week's FOMC meeting," MUFG's Soojin Kim wrote.

Traders broadly expect the Fed to leave interest rates unchanged at its upcoming October 27-28 meeting, but they see a 78% probability of a hike in December, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool.

Two main factors are behind gold's recent swoon, Peter Cardillo of Spartan Capital said in a note - "First, investors are raising cash; second, Russia is selling gold holdings as the war continues to leave its economy in shambles" - but "while the risk of further downside remains, we would selectively buy at these levels."

Front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) for October delivery fell 1.3% on Friday to $3,991.10/oz, its lowest settlement value since July 16, and front-month Comex October silver (XAGUSD:CUR) slumped 1.9% to $53.711/oz, its lowest close since November 26, 2025.

For the week, gold and silver fell 4% and 5.7%, respectively.

SpaceX-related competitive pressure contributed to the slide. Peer TMUS fell 8% as well.T has fallen about 16% in the past month

What Happened to AT&T

Earlier this week, AT&T reported quarterly results. Total revenue grew 5.3%, with service revenue growth of 3.8% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 5.4%. T revealed adjusted EPS of $0.65 for the quarter. 

Wireless service revenue rose 5%, postpaid phone net additions came in at 379,000 with a 0.92% churn rate, and Advanced Home Internet added 696,000 net subscribers, including 416,000 fiber additions and 280,000 Internet Air additions.

Management also said it raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to approximately $2.40 and set a target of more than 60 million fiber locations by the end of the decade, with annual capital investment of $22 billion to $23 billion planned for 2027 and 2028.
